newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa CEO says 1996 profits lower.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa CEO says 1996 profits lower.

text.p: German airlines Deutsche Lufthansa AG 1996 earnings fell short of matching the 756 million marks it earned the year before, but chairman Juergen Weber said in a newspaper interview he was still satisfied.
In an interview published in the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung on Saturday, Weber said 1996 was generally satisfactory in light of higher fuel costs and rising competition in low price areas.
Weber said he expected earnings to rise by around 617 million marks this year and by 1999 earnings could improve by an accumulated 1.3 billion marks.

The improvements in the bottom line would come mainly from savings as a result of restructuring and its alliances. The alliance with United Airlines of the United States brought savings of 80 million marks in its first year, he said.
This year the company would earn an additional 130 million marks as a result of personnel restructuring and improved productivity.
Lower materials costs by purchasing together with other firms, such as its alliance with Scandanavian Airlines, should add an additional 100 million marks.
